comments.headline: Overhead distribution trees violate clearance distances
comments.summary: Proposed Cedar Elm and Live Oak trees are positioned 0–6 feet from the overhead electrical conductor along the southern boundary. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires 15 feet minimum for distribution lines and 25 feet for trees exceeding 40 feet mature height. No Austin Energy approval for non-compliant placements is documented.

details.text: Cedar Elm and Live Oak (non-utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F) are positioned 0–6 feet from overhead distribution conductor, violating 15-foot minimum clearance. Species utility-compatibility not explicitly verified on landscape plan.

runComments.comment: Proposed trees are positioned 0-1.5 feet from overhead electric (OHE) distribution line on southern boundary. Utility-compatibility status of specific tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) cannot be conclusively determined from submitted plans to verify whether species are marked as utility-compatible in ECM Appendix F. ECM Appendix F UC column designation not provided.

Landscape plan shows proposed trees at 3.1 to 6 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor running along southern property boundary. Cedar Elm (non-utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F) and Live Oak (non-utility-compatible) specified on plant schedule are proposed as part of the mitigation trees. Trees must be repositioned to maintain minimum 15 lateral feet from outside conductor per UCM § 1.10.10.4, or species must be changed to utility-compatible alternatives.

Trees are shown planted along the southern site boundary within approximately 5-10 feet of the overhead electric line (based on graphic scale 1"=20'). However, the landscape plan does not identify the species of these trees, so utility-compatible status per ECM Appendix F cannot be verified. Plant species schedule exists on Sheet 35 but is not cross-referenced to specific locations on the landscape plan. Provide species identification labels on the landscape plan for all trees proposed within 25 feet of overhead electric facilities.

details.text: Cedar Elm (90 ft mature) and Live Oak (60 ft mature) exceed 40-foot height threshold requiring 25 feet lateral clearance from distribution conductors. Measured distances of 0–6 feet represent violations of 19–25 feet.

runComments.comment: Large trees with mature height 40+ feet (Cedar Elm and Live Oak per ECM Appendix F) are proposed at 0-1.5 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires minimum 25 lateral feet clearance. Measured distances: 0 feet (westernmost), 1.5 feet (central), 0 feet (easternmost).

Proposed large trees (Cedar Elm at 90 feet mature height, Live Oak at 60 feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) are located 3.1 to 6 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor. Large trees require minimum 25 lateral feet clearance from distribution conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Trees must be repositioned or replaced with trees of compliant mature height (less than 40 feet).

Large trees (mature height 40+ feet) cannot be verified as meeting the 25-foot clearance requirement from distribution conductors because the landscape plan does not identify which species are planted at which locations. While Live Oak and Cedar Elm are shown in the plant schedule with 16-foot minimum heights, their mature heights per ECM Appendix F cannot be verified against specific planting locations on the site plan. Provide species identification and mature height notation on landscape plan for all proposed trees.

details.text: No documented written approval from Austin Energy is provided for trees positioned within prohibited clearance zones or utilizing non-utility-compatible species. Variations require explicit Austin Energy approval per UCM § 1.10.10.4.

runComments.comment: Plans propose trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) within prohibited clearance zones: trees within 15-25 feet of overhead distribution conductors and within 10 feet of utility poles and transformer equipment. No documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing these variations is provided or referenced on the plans, in the site plan notes, or in the submitted documents.

Landscape plan proposes trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) within prohibited clearance zones (less than 15 feet from distribution conductors and less than 25 feet for large trees) without documented written approval from Austin Energy. Variations to standard tree placement distances and non-compatible species designations require explicit Austin Energy approval per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide signed approval letter from Austin Energy or revise landscape plan to maintain required clearances.

comments.headline: Trees violate clearance from utility poles and transformer pads
comments.summary: Proposed trees are measured 1.7–8.5 feet from utility poles and transformer pads, violating UCM § 1.10.10.4 minimum 10-foot lateral clearance. Additionally, poles and transformer access doors are not clearly identified or cross-referenced on the landscape plan.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy for utility pole locations and transformer pad access requirements.

details.text: Proposed tree measured 8.5 lateral feet from utility pole centerline, violating minimum 10-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Utility poles are not clearly identified or labeled on electrical (Sheet 21) or landscape (Sheet 31) plans, preventing verification of all tree-to-pole distances.

runComments.comment: Proposed tree measured at 8.5 lateral feet from overhead electric utility pole. UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of poles. Tree location is 1.5 feet closer than minimum required distance.

Electrical utility poles are not clearly identified or labeled on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) or landscape plan (Sheet 31). Proposed trees must maintain minimum 10 lateral feet from utility pole centerlines per UCM § 1.10.10.4, but this cannot be verified from submitted plans. Provide pole locations and identify all utility poles on the landscape plan with tree locations relative to poles clearly dimensioned or noted.

details.text: Proposed tree measured 1.7 lateral feet from pad-mounted transformer equipment access door, violating minimum 10-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Transformer pad locations (west of Buildings 2, 8 and east of Buildings 4, 7) shown on electrical plan are not cross-referenced on landscape plan.

runComments.comment: Proposed tree measured at 1.7 lateral feet from pad-mounted electrical transformer equipment. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires minimum 10 lateral feet clearance from pad-mounted equipment or between equipment access door and drivable surface. Tree position violates distance requirement by 8.3 feet.

Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations (west of Buildings 2 and 8, east of Buildings 4 and 7), but landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not provide cross-reference or clear notation showing tree locations relative to transformer access doors. Trees must maintain 10 lateral feet from pad-mounted equipment access doors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide dimension or cross-sheet reference showing tree clearances from transformer pads.

comments.headline: Underground electrical equipment clearances not verified
comments.summary: Underground electrical conduits, pull boxes, and transformer equipment are shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) but are not clearly located or dimensioned on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Tree clearances from underground equipment and root barrier requirements cannot be verified.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy for underground equipment locations and clearance specifications.
comments.attn: Cannot verify underground equipment clearance and root barrier compliance from current plans. Findings flagged in single run only; low confidence.

details.text: Underground conduits and pull boxes shown on electrical plan (Sheet 21) are not marked on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Trees must maintain 5-foot minimum lateral clearance from underground electrical equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide location overlay showing underground equipment and adjacent tree clearances.

runComments.comment: Electrical plan shows underground conduits and pull boxes routing through the site, but specific coordinates or dimensions for underground electrical equipment are not provided on the landscape plan. Trees must maintain minimum 5 lateral feet clearance from underground electrical equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide detailed overlay or dimension showing tree locations relative to all underground electrical equipment with 5-foot clearances verified.

details.text: Underground equipment locations are not detailed on landscape plan. Trees within 20 feet of underground electrical equipment require 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Cannot verify which trees fall within affected zones. Provide detailed location plan with equipment zones and root barrier specifications.

runComments.comment: Underground electrical equipment locations are not detailed on landscape plan, preventing verification of which trees fall within the 20-foot root barrier zone. Trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment require minimum 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide detailed location plan showing underground equipment, 20-foot zones, tree locations, and root barrier specifications for any trees within affected zones.

comments.headline: Landscape plan lacks species labels and clearance dimensions
comments.summary: Trees are shown on the landscape plan without species identification labels, mature height notations, or dimensioned clearances from overhead conductors and utility equipment. Plant schedule (Sheet 35) is not cross-referenced to specific tree locations (Sheet 31). Clearance dimensions lack notation of proper measurement reference points.
comments.attn: Some findings flagged in single run only. Verify that all trees within utility clearance zones are properly labeled and dimensioned on landscape plan.

details.text: Trees shown with category symbols (M, SY, PL) without species names. Plant schedule on Sheet 35 lists Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, and Texas Mountain Laurel but is not cross-referenced to Sheet 31 locations. Add species labels to tree symbols for all trees within 50 feet of overhead electrical facilities.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows proposed trees near overhead electric line but identifies them only by regulatory category symbols (M, SY, PL, P) with no species names. Plant schedule exists on Sheet 35 listing species, but landscape plan lacks cross-reference linking specific tree symbols to the species identified on the plant schedule. Proposed trees near utilities must be clearly identified by species directly on the landscape plan or through explicit cross-sheet notation.

The landscape plan does not identify species of trees proposed near overhead electric facilities. Trees are shown with category symbols (M=Mitigation, SY=Street Yard, PL=Parking Lot) and geometric symbols but no botanical or common names are labeled on the plan. While a complete plant schedule exists on Sheet 35 listing Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, and Texas Mountain Laurel with quantities, this schedule is not cross-referenced to specific tree locations on the landscape plan. Add species common names or abbreviations (e.g., 'CE' for Cedar Elm, 'LO' for Live Oak) to tree symbols on the landscape plan for all trees within 50 feet of overhead electric facilities.

details.text: Landscape plan does not distinguish large trees (40+ feet mature height) from smaller species. Cedar Elm (90 ft), Live Oak (60 ft), Mexican Redbud (20 ft), and Texas Mountain Laurel (25 ft) are not differentiated on plan. Large tree species and mature heights must be clearly noted to allow clearance verification.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan does not differentiate large trees (mature height 40+ feet) from smaller trees near overhead electric facilities. Trees shown as 'M' symbols provide no indication of which are Cedar Elm (90 ft), Live Oak (60 ft), or smaller species (Mexican Redbud 20 ft, Texas Mountain Laurel 25 ft). Large tree species and mature heights must be clearly noted or indicated on the landscape plan to allow verification of clearance compliance.

details.text: Overhead electric line and tree symbols visible on landscape plan but not dimensioned. Add dimension lines showing clearance distances from tree trunk centers to outside conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4 measurement methodology (15-foot distribution, 50-foot transmission minimums).

runComments.comment: Trees are shown on landscape plan in relation to overhead electric facilities (OHE line depicted on Sheet 31; transformer pad locations identifiable). However, NO dimension lines, clearance distances, or measurement references are provided on the landscape plan. Clearances cannot be verified from the plan drawings; applicant must add dimension lines and clearance notations from tree trunk centers to outside conductors (for overhead lines) and equipment locations.

The overhead electric line is shown on the landscape plan, but trees are not clearly related to it with dimensions. While both overhead electric lines and tree symbols are visible on Sheet 31, there are no dimension lines, call-outs, or notes indicating clearance distances between the trees and conductors. Sheet 21 shows electrical infrastructure separately from the landscape. Cross-reference the two plans with dimension lines or notes showing clearance distances between trees and overhead conductors, demonstrating compliance with 15-foot (distribution) and 50-foot (transmission) requirements.

details.text: Plan does not dimension clearances from trees to overhead conductors or specify measurement methodology. Clearances must be measured from tree trunk center (planting location symbol) to outside conductor per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide dimensions and reference notes on landscape plan for all trees within utility clearance zones.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan does not show dimensioned clearances between proposed trees and overhead electric conductors. While field measurement identifies distances of 3.1 to 6 feet, plan dimensions and notes must clearly show that all clearances are measured from the outside conductor (not pole centerline) to the tree trunk center (not canopy edge) per UCM § 1.10.10.4 measurement methodology. Provide dimensions on landscape plan showing tree-to-conductor distances measured from proper reference points.

details.text: Clearances between tree trunks and overhead conductors are not dimensioned on landscape plan. Measurement reference points must be tree trunk center per UCM § 1.10.10.4, not projected canopy edge. Provide dimension lines and notes confirming proper measurement methodology from trunk center to outside conductor.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan does not dimension clearances from tree trunks to overhead electric conductors. All clearance measurements must originate from tree trunk center (planting location symbol), not from projected canopy edge per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide dimension lines and notes on landscape plan confirming that clearances are measured from proper reference points.
